chunks: And whatever is in it from Umayyah ibn ʿAmr, from al-Shuʿayrī, I have narrated it from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār—may Allah be pleased with him—from Saʿd ibn ʿAbdullah, from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, from Umayyah ibn ʿAmr, from Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim al-Shuʿayrī.

key_terms.الشُّعَيْرِيِّ: Al-Shuʿayrī; the attributed transmitter named in the chain
key_terms.الْعَطَّارِ: Al-ʿAṭṭār; an identifying epithet within the sanad/isnad
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him; an honorific supplication for the transmitter
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; indicates the author’s direct citation of his transmission route

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to Umayyah ibn ʿAmr from al-Shuʿayrī in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits reports from Umayyah ibn ʿAmr from al-Shuʿayrī. Its significance lies in documenting the transmission route in hadith scholarship and preserving the source chain for verification.
